FAQ

Short answers.

What is Fresh Terminal?

A terminal you talk to in plain words. It answers, and it changes its own menus, pages, layout, theme and skins to fit what you are doing. Every change can be undone.

Do I need to sign up?

No. Open it and type. Your stages are saved in your browser. Sign in with GitHub, Google or email only if you want the $5 starter kit and cloud save.

What does it cost?

Free usage to try (about 40 prompts), then $5 of usage on us when you sign in. After that you will pay what the models cost plus a small fee (5% for now, not final). Paying is not wired yet. With your own key we charge $0 for models.

What is “your key”?

Your own OpenRouter key. Press K in the terminal and paste it. It stays in your browser, calls go straight to OpenRouter, and the provider bills you. You are never blocked. Cloud storage past 100 MB will cost about $0.05 per GB-month (not final, not billed yet).

What happens when free usage runs out?

Sign in for the starter kit, or switch to your own key. Once the starter kit is spent, your key keeps working; pay as you go opens when payments are wired.

Is my data private?

Private from us by default: signed out, your stages stay in your browser. To answer you, a request passes through our router to the model provider (through OpenRouter); the router keeps the cost line, not your words. The provider's own terms apply to what it receives. With your own key, our router is not involved at all.

If you sign in, your stages (menus, pages and looks) are saved in our database so they reach your other devices; your conversation stays in your browser. Encryption at rest with your own key is coming, and so is an optional “share my data” checkbox, off by default. We will only see an account if you grant access.

Can I undo what it changes?

Yes. Every change shows as one line with Undo. Replay shows the whole session step by step, and you can export a session as a file and import it again.

What are stages and tags?

A stage is one workspace: its menu, pages, look and conversation. Tags are the words the terminal recognises as you type (actions, dates, names, lists); tap one to change what it means, and the glossary remembers.

Which models does it use?

A small route table picks a model on OpenRouter for each request, and simple commands run locally for free. Every reply shows the model, the time and the cost.

What is not live yet?

Coming soon: realtime multiplayer, live sync across your devices, voice talk-back, connectors, migration, teams and self-host, and paying as you go. We mark these “coming soon” or “not wired yet” wherever they appear. Already live: a prompt typed while offline waits safely, and you choose to send, edit or discard it when the connection is back.

Is it open?

The source is on GitHub, and FreshStack, the open starter kit, documents every piece of the stack underneath.
